name: wxWidgets
summary: A C++ cross-platform GUI toolkit that presents a common window and event API while adapting controls to native platform toolkits and managing application and event-loop lifecycles.

features.name: Native widget adapter layer
features.description: wxWindow and related public interfaces define portable window and control operations, while platform-specific source directories implement those interfaces for native toolkits. The toolkit therefore exposes a stable application-facing surface with backend-specific behavior behind it.
benefits: Shares application code across supported desktop platforms
Can use native controls and platform conventions
costs: Visual behavior and capabilities can vary by backend
Portable code must respect platform-specific constraints

features.name: Typed event-table routing
features.description: wxEvent defines typed event tags and wxEvtHandler provides event-table and handler machinery. The fixed headers and common implementation show that events are represented as typed values and dispatched through handler tables, with filters and propagation available at the framework boundary.
benefits: Separates platform event production from application handlers
Supports custom event types and reusable handler registration
costs: Dispatch order and propagation rules affect behavior
Handler ownership and lifetime must be coordinated

features.name: Application and event-loop lifecycle
features.description: wxAppConsoleBase defines initialization, run, event-loop entry and exit, and cleanup hooks. Applications enter through this lifecycle rather than directly owning each platform message loop.
benefits: Centralizes startup, dispatch, and shutdown sequencing
Provides lifecycle hooks shared by GUI and base applications
costs: Application work is coupled to framework loop semantics
Nested or platform-specific loop behavior requires care

mathematical_views.question: Which application-facing window and event operations are preserved when wxWidgets maps them to different native backends?
assumptions: wxWindow and wxEvtHandler define the abstract contract
Platform implementations refine the contract rather than exposing identical native behavior
The view does not claim behavioral equivalence for all controls

mathematical_views.question: How do initialization, event dispatch, nested loop entry, and shutdown transition an application through its runtime lifecycle?
assumptions: Lifecycle callbacks are states or transitions
Events are delivered while an active loop is running
The model abstracts OS message-loop details

costs: Routing and lifetime rules add framework coupling
